building.note: The executed ordinance is a 126-page scan, read by OCR and checked against the text-layer draft attached to the same council item. Chapter 18.08 amends Sections 105.2, 107.2.5.2, 202, 310.1, 1109.2.1 (family or assisted-use toilet rooms and baby changing stations), 311.4, 501.2, 1101.2 to 1101.4, 1107.6.1.1.1, 1204.1, 1804.8, 2114, 3107.1, 3201.1, 3305.2 (toilets for construction workers) and 3401, and adopts Appendices C to G and I to K. It does not amend Chapter 8 (interior finishes), Table 1004.5 or Chapter 29 (Sections 2902 and 2903). A 2025 ordinance (Legistar file 25-769) only replaced the Construction Board of Appeals with an appeals officer. The codified text on Municode could not be opened (automated access blocked).

codes.authority: City of El Paso Planning & Inspections Department (the building official; One Stop Shop, 811 Texas Ave.)

amendment.text: El Paso adopts the 2021 International Plumbing Code and leaves Table 403.1, the half-and-half split (403.1.1), the single-user rule (403.1.2), the separate-facilities exceptions (403.2) and the urinal substitution rule (424.2) as printed. Its only change in Section 403 is an added exception to 403.3: a tenancy of 200 square feet or less in a stand-alone building needs no public toilets of its own where it does not handle potentially hazardous food, toilets are available on the same site within 200 feet of travel, and the site as a whole has the required number. The building code's Chapter 29 is not amended. Because Texas has no statewide table, the page needs its own stall table, read from the 2021 code.
amendment.quote: 18.20.040 Section 403.3 Required public toilet facilities, exception added. ... Exception: Small tenancies and areas located in stand-alone buildings or tenancies. Customers, patrons, visitors and employees need not be provided with public toilet facilities in small tenancies located in stand-alone buildings, structures or facilities when all of the following conditions are met: 1. The gross floor area of the tenancy does not exceed 200 square feet; and 2. The building, or structure is not used for the preparation, storage handling and sale of potentially hazardous food ...; and 3. Toilet facilities are provided elsewhere on the same site within 200 lineal feet of travel distance from the exempted tenancy; and 4. The site is provided with the minimum number of facilities required by International Plumbing Code, 2015 Edition, Section 403 and Table 403.1 ...
amendment.note: Condition 4 still cites the 2015 edition in the 2021 ordinance (as printed).

table_ratios.office: Business: water closets 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50 (each sex)
table_ratios.restaurant: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts: 1 per 75 male, 1 per 75 female
table_ratios.split: 403.1.1: "To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. ... Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number."
table_ratios.urinals: None required. 424.2: "In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies."
table_ratios.small_occupancy: 403.2 exception 2: "Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer." Exception 3: mercantile occupancies of 100 or fewer. Exception 4: business occupancies of 25 or fewer.
table_ratios.source: Secondary copy: UpCodes, 'Texas IHB Plumbing Code 2021' (the 2021 International Plumbing Code as adopted by Texas for industrialized buildings; Section 403 reads as the model code). No El Paso copy exists on UpCodes, and the official ICC viewer loads its text by script.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Half the occupants counted as each sex, fractions rounded up (403.1.1). Office at 100: 50 each sex = 2. Office at 200: 100 each sex = 2 for the first 50 plus 1 for the next 50. Office at 400: 200 each sex = 2 + 3. Restaurant at 400: 200/75 = 2.67, so 3. School at 400: 200/50 = 4. Urinals may replace up to 50% of the men's toilets in offices and up to 67% in restaurants (assembly) and schools (424.2).

restrooms_city.rule: El Paso City Code Chapter 5.19 (created by Ordinance No. 019569, passed November 21, 2023, in effect January 1, 2024) requires gender-neutral signage on every single-user restroom in a commercial facility, other than private or private-use restrooms; the person in control of the facility must install and maintain the sign; a violation is a Class C misdemeanor. The adopted 2021 codes say the same of single-user toilet rooms (IPC 403.1.2, IBC 2902.1.2) and allow a room for both sexes with water closet compartments and urinals in stalls or visually separated (403.2 exception 6). El Paso's building code amendment also requires a family or assisted-use toilet room in assembly and mercantile occupancies and a baby changing station on each floor with bathrooms in every new establishment or use (18.08.055). No city rule on shared all-gender rooms beyond the adopted codes was found.
restrooms_city.quote: Section 5.19.020 Applicability. This chapter applies to single-user restrooms within commercial facilities that are not private or private use restrooms. ... Section 5.19.030 Signage Required A. A single-user restroom subject to this article must have gender-neutral signage. B. A person with control over a commercial facility with at least one single-user restroom shall install and maintain gender-neutral signage for each single-user restroom. ... C. "Single-user restroom" means a lockable restroom available for an individual for use with or without assistance. ... Section 4. Title 5, Chapter 5.19 Signage for Single-User Restrooms) shall take effect January 1, 2024. || 18.08.055 Section 1109.2.1 Family or assisted-use toilet and bathing rooms. In assembly and mercantile occupancies, an accessible family or assisted-use toilet room shall be provided. ... Every new establishment or use shall be required to provide a baby diaper changing station in accordance with the requirements of this section. Each establishment or use shall be required to provide at each floor level containing bathrooms, at least one diaper changing station that is accessible to women, and one that is accessible to men, or a single station accessible to both. Each establishment shall provide signage indicating the location of the baby diaper changing station.
restrooms_city.note: Chapter 5.19 was read as enacted, on the executed ordinance; the codified text on Municode could not be opened, so later amendments or a repeal were not checked. The city's own page on the Texas Women's Privacy Act (https://www.elpasotexas.gov/ada/texas-womens-privacy-act/) exists but its body text did not load. Texas Government Code chapter 3002 (state pack) governs city-owned buildings since December 2025. The family-room amendment is numbered 1109.2.1, the section number of earlier editions (1110.2.1 in the 2021 code), and omits the model code's threshold of six or more required water closets.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to El Paso job sites. Price your restroom, pick the right material and see the El Paso and Texas rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for El Paso schools, warehouses, clinics and restaurants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** El Paso's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** El Paso sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
extra_rule_bullets: - **Family restrooms and changing stations:** El Paso's building rules call for a family or assisted-use toilet room in stores and in buildings where people gather. Every new business must also have a baby changing station on each floor that has restrooms, one that women can reach and one that men can reach, or a single one open to both, with a sign showing where it is.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** El Paso requires a permit to alter or repair a building unless the work is on its exempt list. The list covers "similar finish work" and movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high, without naming toilet partitions, so ask the One Stop Shop at El Paso Planning and Inspections whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a lockable one-person restroom in a commercial building must carry a gender-neutral sign. El Paso has required this since January 2024, and the person in charge of the building must put the sign up and keep it there. In a private building, a shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and urinals are in stalls or screened from view. Since December 2025, Texas law requires shared restrooms in city, county, school district and public college buildings to be designated for one sex.
page.stalls_intro: El Paso counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional. They may stand in for up to half of the men's toilets in an office, and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building. An office that holds 25 people or fewer, a store that holds 100 or fewer, or any other space that holds 15 or fewer, staff and customers together, doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or El Paso Planning and Inspections sets the final number.
page.install_rule: A contractor registers with El Paso Planning and Inspections before pulling a building permit. Registration takes an annual fee, proof of insurance and a $50,000 bond. Texas has no statewide contractor license for this work. Confirm what your project needs with El Paso Planning and Inspections. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who pulls a building permit in El Paso must be registered with the City.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on city, county and school district projects, Texas law requires at least the locally set wage. The federal rate for a carpenter on building work in El Paso County is $13.51 an hour plus $3.29 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.25% in El Paso: 6.25% state, 1% city, 0.5% county and 0.5% transit.
page.buyers_extra: - **Truck terminals and border freight buildings:** HDPE or phenolic for driver and crew restrooms that take hard use and washdown.
